about: Origin Engine's style catalogue: 6 looks in the engine's own words, each with what a critic checks on a rendered frame and what it must not hold as a defect (`intended`: the traits that look like defects but are the style, such as hard pixel steps, dither or broken edges; it never names the style, so a blind critic reads it too), the premises it fits, the look preset it maps to (a checked file.look TypeScript declaration; extends: ["<slug>"] in a game's own look builds on it), the built-in UI style its look's ui field names, its variants (one preset drawn another way: variant: "<name>" in a game's look lays templates/looks/variants/<slug>/<name>.ts over the preset; each variant has its own title, descriptor, mood, checks, intended traits, premise, palette, specs, art bible and, where it needs authored art, authored, which the brief and the critic read in place of the look's), palette and asset specs, and an art-bible direction the agent expands per project. `preview` is a picture of the style as a game, 960x540 (previews/<slug>.webp against the root of @origingame/engine/knowledge; not in the platform mount, whose payload is text). `look.layers` names what the style needs: frame (the look's render resources), conform (the cook makes the assets meet the look's art contract), runtime (sprite outline, palette swap, pixel-art rotation, camera presets), authored (art no conformance makes); `look.support` follows from them: full when every layer but authored is implemented, content when authored art is needed, partial otherwise, with `missing` naming what, and a content style's `look.authored` the art it needs, each a kind of the art brief and what it must be (artBrief asks for exactly that, docs/art.md). `category` groups the styles in plain terms (`categories` names each group); `look.views` lists the views it suits (side-2d, top-down-2d, isometric-2.5d, third-person-3d, first-person-3d: the creation choice's words), only those its profiles draw; `look.mood` is the mood its preset is drawn in, one of bright, dark, warm, cold, soft and high-contrast, any of which a game's look may ask for instead (docs/art.md §2.10). The descriptions are original; no game or studio is the reference for a style.
artBibleTemplate: Art bible for {title}. Premise: {premise}. Camera: {camera}; platform and display size: {platform}. Style: {name} ({descriptor}) Direction: {direction} Palette: {palette}. Asset specs: {assets}. UI: the {ui} style the preset names (a `ui` line in the game's look picks another, or the game's own styles/<name>), re-coloured to this palette. Avoid: {avoid}. Proof: og-project.json selects the game's look as {look}, extending "{slug}"; capture the title, play and results screens with og run and check each against: {checks}. Every later asset is made inside this bible; a request for one asset never redesigns the style.

styles.name: Inked comic 3D
styles.descriptor: Volumetric models keep bold outlines, drawn surface marks and exaggerated colour: a comic page given depth.
checks: Thick black outlines on silhouettes and major creases.
Ink marks (hatching or strokes) are painted onto surfaces.
Proportions are exaggerated (oversized hands, heads or weapons).
styles.intended: Thick black outlines, ink strokes painted onto surfaces and exaggerated proportions are the style, not outline artefacts, dirty textures or broken models.

palette.rules: Bold local colours, black ink for all shadow edges.

assets.textureDensity: hand-inked textures, 1 texel per screen pixel

artBible.direction: Comic ink over 3D: heavy outlines, hatched shading painted in, punchy colour, exaggerated shapes.

styles.name: Faceted low poly
styles.descriptor: Visible polygon facets and simplified meshes, broad colour fields in place of textures, depth from silhouettes and layers.
checks: Facets are visible: each triangle shades flat with a hard edge to its neighbour.
Surfaces carry flat colour, not detailed textures.
Depth reads by value: farther layers are lighter or lower in contrast than nearer ones, and the play area keeps full contrast.
styles.intended: Hard edges between flat-shaded triangles and untextured colour fields are the style, not missing smooth normals or missing textures.

palette.rules: Colour per material, gradients only from lighting and fog.

artBible.direction: Planar facets, flat material colours, depth from value and silhouette, fog only beyond the play area, silhouettes designed from few polygons.
avoid: high polygon counts that hide the facets

styles.name: Pixel art
styles.descriptor: Sprites and tiles on a hard pixel grid with ramped shading, parallax layers behind the action and saturated colour; a topdown variant draws the world from above.
checks: Background layers scroll at visibly different rates and never at the playfield's speed.
Shading on sprites steps through 4 to 6 tones per material with no smooth gradients.
Edges stay on the logical pixel grid when the camera moves (compare two captures 1 s apart at 400 %).
styles.intended: Hard single-cell steps on a coarse grid, four to six flat tones per material with no smooth gradient, and outlines broken by light are the style, not banding, missing antialiasing or gaps in the line.

palette.rules: Ramps of 4 to 6 steps; hue-shifted shadows (cooler) and highlights (warmer); saturated accents on characters, calmer backgrounds.

assets.outlinePx: 1 dark pixel, selectively broken by light

artBible.direction: Volume from stepped shading, layered parallax for depth, lively multi-frame animation, saturated colour kept to the characters and pickups so the playfield reads.
avoid: parallax layers that match the playfield speed

variants.name: topdown
variants.title: Top-down tile worlds
variants.descriptor: Overhead or three-quarter tile maps with upright sprites, where steps, cliffs and overlap make height and paths readable.
checks: Walkable floor, walls and drops are distinguishable in a greyscale capture.
Characters are drawn upright and are occluded by tall tiles in front of them (y-sorting works).
Tile seams are invisible: no gaps or bleeding lines between tiles at any camera position.
variants.intended: Hard pixel steps, a repeating tile grid and upright sprites drawn over the top-down map are the style, not aliasing, tiling or perspective errors.

premise.genre: action RPG, tactics, farming and life sims, overhead adventure

palette.rules: Floors desaturated and mid-value; walls darker on their faces; characters most saturated.

assets.spriteScale: 16 x 16 tiles, 16 x 24 to 24 x 32 characters

artBible.direction: A strict tile grid, height told by wall faces and drop shadows, upright characters sorted by their feet, paths readable before decoration.
avoid: decoration on walkable paths that hides edges

styles.name: Neon vector lines
styles.descriptor: Thin glowing lines, grids and bright particles on dark fields, like a vector display.
checks: Mean luminance of a capture is below 0.15 and line pixels are near full brightness.
Lines glow: a halo wider than the line itself (bloom).
Geometry is drawn as lines or wireframes, not filled surfaces.
styles.intended: A nearly black frame, thin full-brightness lines with halos and unfilled wireframe geometry are the style, not underexposure, bloom bleed or missing surfaces.

missing: the line art is content: models built with black faces and emissive hue edges (templates/looks/neon-vector/models); the engine draws every lit material's feature edges and blooms them, but a model's own coloured faces still fill

authored.what: built as line art: near-black faces with one saturated emissive hue a part, so only its edges glow
built as line art: near-black faces, an emissive hue for its outline and one accent, no textures

palette.rules: Each hue one meaning (player, enemy, pickup); white only for the hottest centres.

artBible.direction: Luminous lines on black, grids for space, particle bursts, bloom as the material.

styles.name: Toy 3D
styles.descriptor: Chunky toy pieces of satin plastic with rounded bevelled edges, bright colour and soft contact shadows, seen through a tilt-shift band that blurs the top and bottom of the frame: a world small enough to pick up.
checks: Hard edges read rounded: a bevel catches a highlight along every box edge at play distance.
Surfaces have a satin sheen with soft highlights; no gritty texture, no metal or glass realism.
Pieces touching the ground or each other sit in soft ambient-occlusion shadow, and the frame's top and bottom blur round a sharp middle band, as in a tilt-shift photo of a model.
styles.intended: Rounded edges on simple chunky forms, a smooth satin sheen and bright saturated colour are the style, not missing detail, low-resolution models or oversaturation.

premise.genre: party, platformer, puzzle, builder, kart racing

palette.rules: Clean saturated primaries and pastels, one colour per piece; shadows from light, not from dark paint.

assets.faceBudget: props 500 to 3k triangles, figures under 8k, bevelled
assets.textureDensity: flat colour or simple colour textures up to 32 px

artBible.direction: Everything is a toy: chunky simplified forms, rounded bevels, satin plastic, bright clean colour, soft shadows under a sunny sky.

variants.name: paper
variants.title: Paper craft
variants.descriptor: Folded planes, visible sheet thickness and layered cut paper become the world's construction.
checks: Surfaces are flat planes with crisp folds; no smooth organic curvature.
Paper grain or fibre is visible on lit surfaces.
Layered sheets cast soft contact shadows on the layer behind.
variants.intended: Crisp folds on flat planes, visible fibre and soft contact shadows between stacked sheets are the style, not low-poly faceting, noise or ambient-occlusion bugs.

palette.rules: Colours of real paper stock: muted, slightly warm; white is off-white.

assets.spriteScale: characters as 200 to 600 triangle folded shapes
assets.textureDensity: paper texture 1 texel per screen pixel

artBible.direction: Everything is cut, folded or stacked paper: planar facets, thin edges, soft contact shadows, paper grain.

authored.what: built as folded card: flat sheets with crisp folds, scored edges and visible thickness, no curved surfaces (the paper fold recipe)
built as card sheets folded and stood in layers, crisp creases and flat faces (the paper fold recipe)

styles.name: Cartoon 2D
styles.descriptor: Flat cartoon colour: clean shapes filled with a few tones per material and a dark warm contour round every figure and prop.
checks: Each material is filled with two or three flat tones, stepped in value, with no smooth gradient.
Characters and props carry a dark warm contour, not a pure black one.
Shapes are simple and readable at a glance: no fine painterly texture inside the fills.
styles.intended: Flat fills of a few tones, a warm dark contour round every figure and simple exaggerated shapes are the style, not banding, a halo or missing detail.

premise.genre: platformer, adventure, puzzle, casual, children's games

missing: the drawing is content: characters, props and backdrops drawn as flat-colour cartoon illustration (the engine flattens their tones, holds them to the palette and draws the contour)

authored.what: drawn as a cartoon character: simple exaggerated shapes, flat fills of two or three tones a material, a clean dark warm contour
drawn as a cartoon background: flat colour shapes, simple layered planes, lighter and less contrasted than the characters

palette.rules: Ramps of three tones a material; saturated characters, softer backgrounds; contour a dark warm brown.

artBible.direction: Clean cartoon shapes, flat fills stepped in two or three tones, a warm dark contour, characters brighter than the world behind them.
